html:
Matthias Corvinus was king of Hungary from 1458 to 1490, born in 1443 in Kolozsvár, today's Cluj-Napoca in Romania, whose reign is remembered as the last golden age of the medieval kingdom.

He was the son of John Hunyadi, hero of the siege of Belgrade, and was elected king at 14. He built a paid standing army called the Black Army, fought the Ottomans, took Moravia and Silesia from Bohemia, and in 1485 captured Vienna and ruled from there. At his court in Buda he gathered Italian humanists and built the Bibliotheca Corviniana, one of the largest libraries in Europe of its time. Folk tales remember him as Matthias the Just. After his death the nobles chose weak kings, and Hungary fell to the Ottomans at Mohács in 1526.
